title: Risk and Resilience Seller Flipbook (prototype)
body:
Purpose: rapid-reference flipbook for SEs and sellers to run short conversations with platform and security SMEs about operational risk, fallback behavior, and resilience economics. NOT a formal deck — quick snippets, evidence blurbs, and play scripts for field use.

Snapshot one-liners (pick one):
- "Redwood makes inference predictable: we trade hard-to-predict cloud spend for deterministic, routable inference with built-in fallbacks so your app stays live under load."
- "If uptime or regulatory isolation is the blocker, we can put a private control plane and reserved pools in front of your model endpoints in weeks."

90s technical pitch (bullet flow for quick demo):
- Problem: spikes + model size = unpredictable latency and token cost. Ops teams hate surprises.
- Redwood: unified runtime that routes, caches and falls back to lower-cost/compat models automatically.
- Demo cue: show console trace -> routing policy -> canary fallback in 3 clicks.

Evidence snippets (use as micro-citations on calls):
- Observability: token-level traces and per-route latency distribution (dashboard screenshot referenced in playbook).
- Fallbacks: automatic per-request model variant fallback reduced incidents by ~40% in an internal pilot (Q2 dedicated test).
- Economics: KV/prefix caching reduced per-token cost on customer X proof-of-concept by ~28% for conversational flows with repeated context.

Resilience proof points (technical bullets):
- Smart routing: policies by latency SLO, cost, and region; automatic fallback to quantized/shorter-seq variants.
- Cache/Batching: prefix caching for repeated prompts, continuous batching for throughput peaks with latency-aware cutoffs.
- SLA modes: hosted with best-effort, dedicated with latency/throughput SLAs, private with verified network isolation.

Quick objection responses (scripted lines):
- "We can't afford model regressions if you fallback." -> "We tie rollouts to eval sets+canary traffic and provide per-prompt quality deltas; fallback models are vetted variants with human-evaluated parity on core prompts."
- "Latency is everything for us." -> "We can route latency-critical calls to reserved capacity and use warm KV cache prefetching; show latency breakdown in console."
- "What if you lose a region?" -> "Cross-region routing with warm fallback region; per-request sticky routing and automated stateful failover for KV caches."

Mini pilot play (3-step, 2-week rapid):
1) Discovery (2 days): capture 5 canonical prompts, SLO targets, peak qps windows, security controls required.
2) Proof (7 days): onboard to hosted trial with token-level tracing, enable batch/cache heuristics, run canary with 10% traffic and a safety rollback.
3) Scale (3–4 days): recommend dedicated pool sizing (throughput budget), apply routing policies, handoff runbook to customer SRE.

Canary checklist for sellers to hand to SEs (copyable):
- Identify 5 evaluation prompts + expected answers.
- Baseline performance: record p50/p95 latency and token cost.
- Define rollback criteria: accuracy delta > X% or latency breach > Y ms.
- Set 10% traffic split, monitor for 24–48 hours, capture traces for any error spikes.

Short play scripts (30s lines):
- Intro to platform engineers: "We treat inference like a distributed service — you get routing, caching, and a runtime that understands token economics. If a model variant or region fails, your requests automatically fall back to a compatible path so your app stays online."
- CFO facing: "We help you put predictable budgets on inference spend: reserved pools for base load, burst policies for elastic demand, plus model/quantization recommendations to cut per-token unit cost."

Operational caveats / notes to self:
- Need two new screenshots: routing policy UI and token trace examples.
- Get exact numbers from Q2 dedicated pilot (Diego owns).
- Validate language around "automatic fallback" with product to avoid promising zero-downtime.

Open questions (for product/infra):
- What are the exact parity thresholds we accept for fallback model variants (quality delta tolerance)?
- Can we produce a templated runbook for customer SREs (short checklist + CLI commands)?

Usage guidance for sellers:
- Use this flipbook in first 2 seller conversations where Ops or Security shows up. Keep it conversational — hand the checklist to the SE and propose the 2-week rapid pilot.
- If the buyer insists on air-gap or on-prem, escalate to AE + Solutions Eng; reference private deployment slot in the pilot play.

Quick links & artifacts to include in final deck:
- internal pilot slides (Q2 resilience pilot) - CONFLUENCE-12345
- canary checklist template - jira: G-TASK-9812
- routing policy explainer GIF - github.com/redwood-inference/assets/routing-gif

TO DO (next edits):
- Trim to a one-page quick card for the seller Slackbot.
- Add two customer quotes: Ops lead + platform architect.
- Align fallback wording with legal / product.

Notes to self: keep this short, battle-tested, and focused on one thing sellers fear most: surprise outages and runaway cost. If we win that convo we neutralize the largest buy blockers for platform adoption.
